sense: clear oneself or another of blame

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; sē pūrgāre alicui
evidence: Cic. Fam. 12.25.3: quod tē mihi dē Semprōniō pūrgās, accipiō excūsātiōnem (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Am. 3.2.28: ut mē pūrgārem tibi (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The figurative sense of “clean”: to clear someone of a charge, sē alicui dē aliquā rē pūrgāre (Lewis & Short).
To excuse a person or a fault, or to plead something as one’s excuse: valētūdinem excūsāre (Liv. 6.22) (Lewis & Short).
Of speech, to argue for something, or to allege it in one’s defence (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quod tē mihi dē Semprōniō pūrgās, accipiō excūsātiōnem
phrases.english: as for your justifying yourself to me about Sempronius, I accept the excuse

sources: Lewis & Short: purgo · Lewis & Short: excuso · Lewis & Short: defendo
